title: Smallness and extension closure of the maximal alpha-compact class
statement: Let C be a locally v-small triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with v-small coproducts. Let G be essentially v-small and shift-closed, consist of alpha-small objects, satisfy G4 [def-sfb-alpha-compact-object], and generate C as a localizing class. For regular alpha, the maximal class alphaCompactObjects C alpha is essentially v-small and closed under middle vertices of distinguished triangles.

source.place: Krause (2001), Lemma 5 pages 124--125 and the maximal-class construction; Localization theory 6.2--6.3.

proof.text: The canonical maximal alpha-compact class S is replete, contains zero, and is shift closed by the API. The extension lemma makes it triangulated, and its bounded-coproduct closure is already proved. Since G is alpha-small and satisfies G4, the existential definition gives G contained in S.
Apply the small bounded triangulated hull theorem to G inside S. This gives an essentially v-small replete triangulated class H between G and S, closed under coproducts of fewer than alpha objects.

Apply the localizing factor-through argument and the assumed generation property to obtain S contained in the retract closure of H. Mathlib proves that retract closure of an essentially v-small class in a locally v-small category is essentially v-small. Essential smallness passes to subclasses. The already proved extension closure gives the second conjunct.

proof_origin.place: Krause (2001), Lemma 5, pages 124–125; finite extension closure proves maximal-class extension closure, the transfinite small hull and localizing factor-through argument give the size bound via retracts.
